exposure: Gestational age at birth (23 weeks vs. 24-26 weeks)
cohort: 125 infants born at either 23 weeks (n=34) or 24-26 weeks (n=91) gestation
finding: For infants born at 23 weeks gestation with indications for cesarean section, vaginal birth was associated with a higher risk of poor neonatal outcomes, including death or cerebral palsy.
mod_finding: Cesarean section for obstetrical indications at 23 weeks gestation may improve neonatal outcomes compared to vaginal birth.
